inspect_bundle.description: Open Graph ran, via the command, the Open Bundle Issues command, a target switch in the panel, the status bar or the sidebar.

properties.from_resource_file: Whether it was started from a resource file that include loads, not from databricks.yml. No path is sent.
properties.outcome: ok | ok_with_errors | no_bundle_file | cli_not_found | cli_not_executable | validation_timeout | validation_output_too_large | invalid_bundle_shape | validation_failed | exception
properties.cli_outdated: Whether the Databricks CLI is older than the oldest tested version (v0.299.0). Not sent when no CLI was found.
properties.cli_version: The Databricks CLI's major and minor version, e.g. 1.21. Not sent when no CLI was found or its version isn't a plain number.
properties.has_diagnostics: Failed inspections only: whether the CLI reported file diagnostics.
properties.fell_back_to_probe: Whether the requested target failed and a structural preview was shown instead.
properties.fallback_reason: Fell back only: why, as one fixed word, never the message: timeout | not_logged_in | no_profile | several_profiles | other_workspace | no_such_target | login_unreachable (the login needed renewing and Databricks couldn't be reached) | login_expired | login_other | other
properties.target_count: Number of targets, as a range (0, 1, 2-5, 6-20, 21-50, 51+).
properties.job_count: Number of jobs, as a range.
properties.task_count: Number of tasks, as a range.
properties.task_kinds: Databricks task type keys present, e.g. notebook_task,sql_task.
properties.issue_count: Number of inspector issues, as a range.

extension_activated.description: The extension started, once per VS Code window. It starts by itself when the open folder contains a bundle file, or when one of its commands is run.

properties.bundle_count: Number of bundles found in the open folders, as a range.
properties.bundle_at_root: Whether a bundle file sits at the top of an open folder.
properties.cli_found: Whether the Databricks CLI could be run. Not sent when no bundle was found, because nothing was checked.
properties.cli_version: The Databricks CLI's major and minor version, e.g. 1.21. Sent only when it could be run and its version is a plain number.
properties.issue_count: Number of errors and warnings the first check put in the Problems panel, as a range. Not sent when nothing was checked.

bundle_refreshed_on_save.description: The open inspector refreshed after a bundle-related file was saved.

properties.bundle_file: Whether the saved file was databricks.yml itself.

file_opened.description: A file was opened from the inspector.

properties.file_kind: py | ipynb | sql | yml | json | whl | jar | scala | r | other

review_summary_copied.description: The bundle review summary was copied.

graph_mode_changed.description: The graph was switched between all tasks and issues only.

job_selected.description: A different job was picked in the header.

search_result_selected.description: A task was picked from search results.

issue_item_selected.description: An item in the issues panel was clicked.

quick_fix_applied.description: A suggested fix was applied from the Quick Fix menu.

bundle_progress.description: Once a day, for the previous day the extension checked bundles: whether findings were resolved. Each bundle's errors and warnings at the start of the day are compared with its last complete check, on this machine. Checks on another branch, extension version or Databricks CLI version are not compared. Never sends which bundle or which findings.

properties.comparison: compared (two complete checks of the same bundle under the same conditions) | not_comparable (only first checks or checks after a change of branch or version) | check_incomplete (only checks that failed or could not read every finding)
properties.resolved: compared only: findings gone while their task, resource or file is still in the bundle, as a range.
properties.new: compared only: findings that were not there at the start, as a range.

sidebar_opened.description: The Databricks Bundle Inspector sidebar showed for the first time in a VS Code window. Once per window.

properties.at_start: Whether it showed within 5 seconds of the extension starting, which usually means VS Code reopened it as it was left. Someone opening it in those first 5 seconds is counted the same way.

sidebar_action.description: A row or button of the sidebar was used: each one at most once per VS Code window, so it says whether it is used, not how often. The same commands run from the Command Palette are not counted here.

properties.action: open_graph | open_problems | pick_problem (a problem picked from the list of several) | open_target | open_bundle_file | check_again | check_all | choose_cli | choose_profile

extension_uninstalled.description: Sent once by the vscode:uninstall hook, only if the extension last recorded that usage telemetry was enabled.

commonProperties.common.*: Added by VS Code's TelemetryLogger: extension name and version, VS Code version, commit and release date, product, UI kind, remote type, whether VS Code was newly installed. Not the VS Code session ID. Only these listed keys are kept; machine and device IDs (common.vscodemachineid, common.sqmid, common.devDeviceId) are removed.
commonProperties.install_id: Added by the proxy: the event's pseudonymous distinct_id, copied so PostHog filters can match it.
commonProperties.common.appname: Host editor name, e.g. Visual Studio Code or Cursor.
commonProperties.common.os: Operating system: darwin, win32 or linux.
commonProperties.common.arch: CPU architecture, e.g. arm64 or x64.
